What are we building?
Hard Rock Digital is focused on becoming the best online sportsbook, casino, and social gaming company in the world. We’re building a place that resonates passion for learning, operating and building new products and technologies for millions of consumers. We care about each customer's interaction, experience, behavior, and insight and strive to ensure we’re always acting authentically.

Rooted in the kindred spirits of Hard Rock and the Seminole Tribe of Florida, the new Hard Rock Digital taps a brand known the world over as the leader in gaming, entertainment, and hospitality. We’re taking that foundation of success and bringing it to the digital space — ready to join us?

What’s the position?
A Principal Backend Engineer at Hard Rock Digital is a hands-on engineering leadership (IC) position.
As a Principal Backend Engineer you will:

• 
Be a technical point of contact for various stakeholders.

• 
Be hands-on in both coding and architecture, leading from the front.

• 
Partner closely with Engineering and Product leadership to shape roadmaps and make high-quality trade-offs that maximise business and customer impact.

• 
Mobilise the team around high-impact problems, creating clarity, alignment and momentum, injecting urgency when needed, or slowing things down to ensure safety and long-term sustainability.

• 
Lead and influence architectural direction for the most complex systems, ensuring cohesive and scalable designs

• 
Set and uphold a high bar for technical excellence across the team, driving improvements in quality, readability and scalability, and fostering a culture where engineers hold each other to that standard.

• 
Proactively mentor, sponsor and develop senior engineers, multiplying your impact by enabling others to operate at a higher level.

• 
Leading and influencing engineers in the team without direct authority – through code, design reviews and technical mentorship

• 
Spotting and resolving cross-team technical dependencies before they become blockers

• 
Champion the adoption of AI-assisted development practices and tools across the team, helping raise the bar on engineering velocity and code qual

Requirements
What are we looking for?

• 
Demonstrable experience operating at staff or principal level

• 
Deep backend engineering expertise with a track record of designing and building distributed systems at scale

• 
The kind of judgment that earns trust fast – engineers follow your technical lead because you’re right, not because of your title

• 
Experience with Java is a strong advantage; we’re less concerned about specific languages that we are about depth of backend systems thinking

• 
Solid understanding of Core account infrastructure and geolocation flows

• 
Strong written and verbal communication; you can make complex technical decisions legible to non-technical stakeholders

• 
Hands-on experience using AI-assisted development tools (e.g. GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor) in your day-to-day workflow, with a genuine enthusiasm for how AI is changing software engineering, and a track record of championing AI-assisted practices — in software development, system design, testing, operations, or troubleshooting — while understanding their limitations and trade-offs.

• 

Degree in computer science, a related field, or equivalent work experience (10+ years)

What’s in it for you?
We offer our employees more than just competitive compensation. Our team benefits include:

• 
Competitive pay and benefits

• 
Flexible vacation allowance

• 
Flexible work from home or office hours

• 
Startup culture backed by a secure, global brand

• 
Opportunity to build products enjoyed by millions as part of a passionate team

Roster of Uniques
We care deeply about every interaction our customers have with us, and trust and empower our principal to own and drive their experience. Our vision for our business and customers is built on fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment where regardless of background or beliefs you feel able to be authentic and bring all your talent into play. We want to celebrate you being you (we are an equal opportunities employer).

Hitachi Solutions, Ltd., headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, is a core member of Information & Telecommunication Systems Company of Hitachi Group and a recognized leader in delivering proven business and IT strategies and solutions to companies across many industries. Job Description

Job Description: 

We are looking for a Python Backend Engineer to join our Product Development team. This is a role focused on innovation, engineering excellence, and making the cloud easier for our customers.

Our Python Engineering role is a full-time position dedicated to designing and building microservices (and APIs) that deliver SaaS and PaaS experiences, underpinning our enterprise Analytics as a Service (AaaS) product and other initiatives.

In this role, you will design and build Python microservices, APIs, and packages leveraging FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, and related tools in Django and Flask. We are looking for candidates with a strong software engineering background, ideally with 4+ years in Python development and modern architectures.

Responsibilities

• Write clean, reusable code complete with comments, unit tests, and documentation.
• Collaborate closely with team members across engineering, delivery, QA, product, and design.
• Build secure, scalable back-end systems that deliver real-world value.
• Stay curious and up-to-date on emerging technologies.
• Promote usability best practices and code reusability.

Qualifications

Qualifications & Skills

• Experience: At least 5 years of relevant software development experience, including 4+ years with Python 3.x, Django/Flask Frameworks, Celery, FastAPI (or other standard industry API), and relational databases (SQL/ORM).
• Architecture: Experience with microservices-based architecture and modern cloud-based architecture is essential.
• Problem Solving: Demonstrated ability to take complex requirements and develop them into working features with minimal oversight.
• Cloud Platforms: Experience with the Azure cloud platform, including development and deployment practices, is desired (knowledge of other cloud platforms is also acceptable). Familiarity with Azure Data Factory and Databricks is also highly valued.
• Front-End: Experience with front-end frameworks such as React or Angular is a plus.
• Integration: Competency in performing integrations into enterprise applications.
• Quality: A strong commitment to writing reliable, scalable, testable, and maintainable code.
• Work Style: Self-motivated with a drive to complete tasks within realistic time frames.
• Communication: Ability to communicate clearly both verbally and in writing.
• Collaboration: Capable of working well within teams while maintaining effectiveness as an independent contributor.

Additional Information

Beware of scams

Our recruiting team may communicate with candidates via our @hitachisolutions.com domain email address and/or via our SmartRecruiters (Applicant Tracking System) notification@smartrecruiters.com domain email address regarding your application and interview requests. 

All offers will originate from our @hitachisolutions.com domain email address. If you receive an offer or information from someone purporting to be an employee of Hitachi Solutions from any other domain, it may not be legitimate.

**Design and integrate APIs** for client projects, particularly in real estate marketing and lead generation systems - **Manage AI agent workflows** using tools like Claude Code, Cursor, or similar—knowing when to let AI run and when to intervene - 1443c4307d144005.description: ## About the role We build software that law firms and in-house legal teams rely on to do work that has real consequences if it goes wrong. That puts unusual weight on the backend: multi-tenant data that must stay isolated, document processing jobs that run for minutes rather than milliseconds, permission rules that mirror how legal teams actually share work, and audit trails that need to hold up under scrutiny. We're looking for a third-year engineering student to join us as a Backend Developer Intern. You'll be writing code that ships — features, fixes, and improvements to the systems behind our products — alongside a small team where your work is reviewed carefully and your questions get answered properly. This is not a shadowing role. You'll own scoped pieces of real work end to end, from understanding the problem to seeing it in production. ## What you'll work on - **Product features** — building API endpoints and the business logic behind them, integrating with what the frontend needs. - **Data modelling** — designing schemas that represent how legal work actually happens, and evolving them safely once real data is in them. - **Background processing** — long-running and scheduled jobs for document handling, notifications, and data pipelines, including the retry and failure behaviour that makes them trustworthy. - **Access control** — authentication and fine-grained authorization across tenants, roles, and shared resources. Getting this wrong in legal software is not a small bug. - **Performance** — finding and fixing the slow query, the N+1, the endpoint that falls over on a large document set. - **Reliability** — tests that catch real regressions, and the debugging work of tracing a production error back to the line that caused it. ## What you'll do **Write and ship code** - Build features in Python and Django, exposed through our API layer (REST and GraphQL), with PostgreSQL underneath. - Write reusable, testable code, and the tests that go with it — unit tests for logic, integration tests for the paths that matter. - Move work that doesn't belong in a request cycle into background tasks with Celery, and reason about idempotency, retries, and what happens when a job fails halfway. - Work through the ORM deliberately: understand the SQL your queries generate, and why the convenient version is sometimes the expensive one. **Design before building** - Turn a loosely defined requirement into a concrete plan — data model, API shape, edge cases, and what could go wrong — and get feedback on it before writing the implementation. - Write database migrations that are safe to run against a live system, and reversible when they aren't. - Think about security and data protection as part of the design rather than a review checkbox: input validation, authorization at the right layer, and no leaking data across tenant boundaries. **Collaborate** - Work in Git and GitHub the way the team does — small focused pull requests, useful descriptions, responsive to review, and green CI before merge. - Give and take code review. Reading other people's code closely is one of the fastest ways to get better at writing your own. - Coordinate with frontend engineers on API contracts, and with product on what the requirement actually means before you build to it. **Debug and learn** - Investigate production errors and performance issues using logs, traces, and error reports, and follow them to the actual root cause rather than the first plausible one. - Document what you built and what surprised you, so the next person doesn't rediscover it. - Ask questions early. Two hours stuck is normal; two days silently stuck is not. ## What we're looking for **Core** - Currently in the third year of a B.E. or B.Tech programme. - Solid Python. You're comfortable with functions, classes, modules, and error handling, and you can read code you didn't write. - Working knowledge of relational databases and SQL — joins, indexes, and why a query might be slow. - Understanding of how the web works: HTTP, requests and responses, status codes, and what an API actually is. - Familiarity with Git, and at least basic experience collaborating through GitHub. - Some experience building something that runs — a project, a college assignment taken past the deadline, a tool you wrote for yourself. What it is matters less than that you finished it. - Clear communication. You can explain what your code does and what you're stuck on. **Strong signals (not requirements)** - Experience with Django or another web framework, and with an ORM. - Having written tests you weren't required to write. - Exposure to background job processing, caching, or message queues. - Understanding of authentication and authorization — sessions, tokens, roles, permissions. - Familiarity with Docker, CI pipelines, or cloud platforms. You won't own infrastructure here, but knowing roughly how your code gets deployed helps. - Open-source contributions, technical writing, or a project you can talk about in detail. - Any exposure to the legal, compliance, or regulatory domain. **How you work** - Self-starting and comfortable with ambiguity — requirements here are rarely fully specified up front. - Detail-oriented. Backend bugs are quiet; they show up in someone's data weeks later. - A team player with good time management, who communicates progress and blockers without being asked. - Honest about what you don't know yet. We're hiring an intern, not someone pretending to be a senior engineer. ## How we'll evaluate you Two stages. First, we send you a task — a scoped backend problem close to the kind of work you'd actually do here. Then a technical round, where we go through what you built: the choices you made, the ones you rejected, how you tested it, and how you'd extend it. We care more about your reasoning than about whether every requirement was met. A clean, well-explained partial solution beats a complete one you can't defend. If you have existing projects, send them along — a repository, a write-up, or a demo. Code we can read tells us more than a list of technologies.
